purpose: Prove that the primitives the side-load notification surface depends on actually work on the authoring machine, before any product task claims them. Run before NT-6 and cited by NT-6 and NT-9.

subject.source: npm registry, installed into a scratch directory outside the repository

steps.name: window-created
steps.detail: BrowserWindow with frame:false, transparent:true, resizable:false, skipTaskbar:true, alwaysOnTop:true, show:false, focusable:false, hasShadow:false, webPreferences:{contextIsolation:true,nodeIntegration:false,sandbox:true}

steps.name: card-document-loaded
steps.detail: a card document loaded and rendered in the window

steps.name: shown-without-focus
steps.detail: showInactive() made the window visible without focusing it

steps.name: card-has-painted-content
steps.detail: {"w":320,"h":37} — real laid-out content, not a blank surface

steps.name: card-persists-3s
steps.detail: the card was still present and visible after 3s

conclusions: A transparent, frameless, always-on-top, taskbar-skipping host window is creatable and controllable on this machine.
The card is a DOM document, not a canvas: content laid out to real measured pixels, so APX-CON-07's canvas-plus-DOM-mirror obligation does not apply to the surface.
showInactive() delivers a notification without stealing keyboard focus from the developer's current work.
Click-through is available, so a card can be invisible to the pointer until it is hovered.
screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea reports a 32px top inset on this desktop, so positioning must respect work-area insets rather than assume a full-screen rectangle.
The Electron Tray module and nativeImage construction are both available, so the existing NT-3 tray bridge is buildable on this machine.
GPU process launch failed under software rendering. Irrelevant for a two-line DOM card and recorded rather than worked around.

blockingFinding.observed: Chromium aborts at startup with a setuid-sandbox FATAL: the npm-installed chrome-sandbox helper is owned by the installing user with mode 0755, and the process refuses to run rather than continuing unsandboxed.
blockingFinding.secondAttempt: Renaming the helper away does not fall back to the unprivileged user-namespace sandbox on this machine: kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone is 1, but Ubuntu 24.04's AppArmor unprivileged_userns_restrictions profile blocks it, producing 'No usable sandbox!'.
blockingFinding.consequence: An unprivileged per-user Electron install on Ubuntu 23.10 and newer must launch with --no-sandbox, or a privileged install must provide a root-owned mode-4755 chrome-sandbox. A user-level npm install cannot produce the latter.
blockingFinding.decisionRequired: NT-6 must choose and document the launch policy explicitly, and assert it in a test, rather than letting the packaged app die at startup or silently disabling a sandbox. Note that webPreferences { contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false, sandbox: true } is a renderer-level setting and remains in force independently of the Chromium process sandbox.
blockingFinding.notClaimed: This probe says nothing about macOS or Windows window-manager behaviour. No claim about those platforms is made or implied by this file.

method.script: A single Electron main-process script created in a scratch directory outside the repository. It asserted each primitive, wrote a machine-readable report, and exited non-zero on any failed step.
method.noPathReportedSuccessWithoutRunning: The report was written only after all twelve steps executed; a missing report is itself a failure signal.
